english.title: Importer fail to ensure compliance with regulations before placing civil explosive on market
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the importer of a civil explosive, namely **(..SPECIFY EXPLOSIVE..), failed to ensure, before placing it on the market, that

(A)_[a relevant conformity assessment procedure had been carried out by the manufacturer]_
(B)_[the manufacturer had drawn up the technical documentation]_
(C)_[it bore the UK marking and was accompanied by the required documents in that **(..SPECIFY NON-COMPLIANCE..)]_
(D)_[the manufacturer had complied with the requirements, where applicable, set out in regulation 44 of the Explosives Regulations 2014 relating to the traceability of certain civil explosives excluded from the scope of regulations 33, 34 and 36 in that **(..SPECIFY NON-COMPLIANCE..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 48 of the Explosives Regulations 2014 and section 33(1)(c) and (2) of, and paragraph 7(m) of Schedule 12 to, the Health and Safety at Work Act etc. 1974.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: This offence applies from the 1st January 2021. For the offence applying before this date, see H20697.
